Through: Mr.Mohit Mathur, Seni
 with Mr.Sushil Ku
 Advocate.

versus
 State (Nct Of Delhi)

Through: Mr.Mukesh Kr, App for
 with Si Sunita Ma
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna
 Order

This petition is filed challenging the order dated 20.03.2023 passed in FIR No.98/2023 under Section 376 IPC registered at PS IGI Airport, New Delhi, thereby dismissing an application preferred by the present petitioner seeking permission to travel Israel from 22.03.2023 to 20.04.2023 to attend marriage ceremony of his daughter; to attend passover festival (Israel festival)
and for making necessary arrangements for his family.

2. Admittedly, the date of incident is 18.02.2023 and the petitioner has since been granted regular bail by the learned Trial Court vide order dated 15.03.2023 but with a condition, if the petitioner intends to leave the country, he would take permission of this Court.
When such permission was applied, it was rejected vide order dated 20.03.2023.

It is submitted the petitioner is inclined to give sound surety to the learned Trial Court and as the marriage of his daughter is fixed for 23.03.2023 and as he has to get his knee operated and as he need to attend passover festival at Israel between 05.04.2023 to 13.04.2023, he may be granted permission to travel abroad.

3. The petitioner is employed in a company which has an office at Delhi and the company has also given an undertaking to the Embassy of Israel at New Delhi stating interalia they shall endeavour to see the petitioner return on or before 20.04.2023.

4. The learned senior counsel for the petitioner refers to Annexure-P7 viz. a letter dated 19.03.2023 to say the Embassy of Israel at New Delhi has supported the submissions made by the petitioner stating interalia he may be allowed to visit Israel on humanitarian grounds.

sentences.text: On the other hand the learned APP for the State submits sound sureties may be furnished by the petitioner.

6. In the circumstances, the petitioner is allowed to visit Israel subject to his furnishing two sureties for a sum of Rs.1.00 lac each to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court/Investigating Officer/SHO concerned.
The petitioner shall return to India on or before 20.04.2023 and shall intimate his arrival to the Investigating Officer/SHO concerned.
Let a fresh undertaking be taken from the employer of petitioner qua assurance that the petitioner shall return to India on or before 20.04.2023.
The Investigating Officer/SHO concerned is directed to return the passport of the petitioner seized by them, forthwith against receipt.
7. In view of the above, the petition stands disposed of along with pending application(s).
8. A copy of this order be given dasti under the signature of the Court Master.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
